newsitem.title: CANADA: CI Fund Management announcement/yr results.
newsitem.headline: CI Fund Management announcement/yr results.

text.p: C.I. FISCAL 1997 CASH FLOW UP 21%, REVENUES TOTAL $147 MILLION
TORONTO, Aug. 6 /CNW/ - C.I. Fund Management Inc. today released audited financial results for the twelve months ended May 31, 1997.

Total revenues of $146.8 million for the twelve months ended May 31, 1997 were up 21% from the $121.1 million reported in the same period in the prior fiscal year. Operating cash flow was $45.1 million or $2.74 per common share for the period, up 21% from $37.4 million or $2.27 per common share in the same period in fiscal 1996. This increase reflects the 19% growth in assets under management which at May 31, 1997 were $6.51 billion, up from $5.47 billion at May 31, 1996 (this includes the C.I. Covington Fund which is not listed as a mutual fund under IFIC reporting). Operating cash flow is reported net of $8.8 million of principal repaid in C.I.'s off balance sheet securitization. If this debt were on the balance sheet, the principal repayment would not be reported as a reduction to operating cash flow.

Net income was $9.5 million ($.58 per common share) for the twelve months ended May 31, 1997 compared to $10.5 million ($.64 per common share) for the twelve months ended May 31, 1996. Amortization of deferred sales commissions financed from C.I.'s cash resources were $26.4 million for the twelve months compared to $11.8 million in the prior fiscal year. (The amortization of deferred sales commissions is a result of C.I.'s policy to amortize commissions over 36 months which in turn has a short-term impact on accounting earnings.)

During the twelve months, C.I. financed $45.6 million in deferred sales charge commissions which was provided primarily by C.I.'s $45.1 million operating cash flow. At May 31, 1997, 35.3% of total assets under management have been financed with internal cash resources having a current redemption value of $102.7 million or $6.27 per share. As at May 31, 1997, cash, short-term investments and marketable securities totalled $12.1 million. Principal outstanding on C.I.'s off balance sheet securitization at May 31, 1997 was $38.5 million and will be fully repaid by February 1, 2001.

C.I.'s operating profit margin was .98% of assets under management for the twelve month period ending May 31, 1997, the same as in the prior fiscal year. (Operating profit margin is defined as management fees charged to mutual funds, less selling, general and administrative (SG&A'') expenses net of expenses charged to mutual funds, investment adviser fees and trailer fees but excluding expenses relating to sales commissions).
Details of the operating profit margin are as follows:
(1) Management fee revenues from mutual funds were 1.96% for the twelve
months ending May 31, 1997, down from 1.97% in the prior fiscal year
due to a shift in asset mix to more conservative funds.
(2) Net SG&A expense was .25% for the twelve months ending May 31, 1997,
unchanged from .25% in the prior fiscal year. This level is in line
with targets presented at C.I.'s annual meeting in October, 1996.
(3) Investment adviser expense fees were .23% for the period, down from
.24% in the prior fiscal year due to the economies of higher asset
(4) Trailer fee expenses were .50% for the twelve month period,
unchanged from .50% in the prior fiscal year.
Review of the Three Months ended May 31, 1997.

Revenues for the quarter ended May 31, 1997 were $39.8 million, up from $33.2 million in the similar quarter in fiscal 1996. Operating cash flow was $13.4 million or $.82 per share for the quarter, up 22% from the $11.0 million or $.67 per share for the quarter ended May 31, 1996.

Cash flow from operations was sufficient to finance the $12.3 million paid in deferred sales commissions during the quarter. Earnings per share were $.18 for the three months ended May 31, 1997, down from $.21 for the quarter ended May 31, 1996. The decrease was due to the increase in amortization of deferred sales commissions.

During the quarter, C.I.'s industry-specific funds were the top performers among C.I. funds, led by the Global Health Sciences Fund, up 7.8% and Global Financial Services Fund, up 6.2%. Global markets also continued their strong performance with the C.I. American RSP Fund up 6.1%, the Hansberger Value Fund up 6.0%, the C.I. Global Fund up 5.5%, the Hansberger European Fund up 5.1%, the Hansberger International Fund up 5.0%, and the C.I. Latin American Fund up 4.3%. This strong performance in global equity markets was especially beneficial to C.I., given its extensive line-up of international mutual funds. Overall performance growth for C.I. during the quarter was $155 million or 2.5% of assets under management. The strong growth in C.I's international funds were mitigated in part by the lacklustre performance of domestic equity markets during the quarter.

Net sales for the quarter ended May 31, 1997 were $82 million, down $33 million from the fourth quarter of the prior fiscal year. However, gross sales for the quarter ended May 31, 1997 were $376 million, up from the $323 million in gross sales in the similar quarter in the prior fiscal year. The 16% increase in gross sales on a year-over-year basis came from the Hansberger Value Series which accounted for $88 million of gross sales during the quarter. At May 31, 1997, Hansberger assets totalled $840 million.

At August 6, 1997 total assets under management were $7.2 billion, up over 10% from their level at May 31, 1997. Net sales were $139 million in July, 1997, up from $33 million in June, 1997. Sales of C.I.'s new Harbour Funds and the Hansberger Value Series were responsible for the sales growth.
The Board of Directors today declared a quarterly dividend of $0.04 per common share payable September 15, 1997 to shareholders of record on September 1, 1997.
